description:
Einstein summation for C++23: one immutable object, one call
operator, the result back by value in the operands' own type, every failure
through std::expected and nothing in any header that throws. The subscript can
reach a template parameter -- where a bad one is a static_assert carrying the
sentence rather than a template backtrace, and the contraction path is chosen
during constant evaluation -- or be parsed at run time. Native x64 package: the
public headers plus einsum_rt.dll and einsum_rt.lib in Release and Debug, with
the Boost 1.92, Eigen 3.4 and kokkos/mdspan header subsets the public interface
reaches bundled in, so a consumer needs no other package. Consumers compile with
/std:c++latest and need MSVC 19.38 (Visual Studio 17.8) or newer for
<expected>, std::views::enumerate and std::from_range. The binaries require
AVX2. Only the run-time subscript parser is compiled; the rest of the library,
the whole compile-time planner included, is headers.
